title: Same Judgment, Different Yes: Measuring Multilingual Judgment Profiles in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.28066v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multilingual evaluations often score a model's opening yes or no, a token that also carries model and language answering conventions. We ask when different ways of eliciting and reading an answer recover the same judgment, and when they measure an answer habit. We collect 1.1 million replies from eight models in six languages on up to 105 moral vignettes, varying the question's form, the answer constraint, and the reading of the reply, token or sentence, in both wordings (the FAR-6 battery). Story-level judgment profiles converge across the tested readouts and question forms, except for the yes/no token after a negative interrogative read under a preset mapping: on the same replies, token and sentence profiles agree at a median r = 0.67 across cells, while sentence profiles agree with free-sentence profiles at 0.94, a known linguistic variability. translated_title: 同样的判断，不同的“是”：度量语言模型中的多语言判断画像
translated_abstract: 多语言评估通常对模型回答开头的是/否标记进行打分，而这个标记同时也承载着模型和语言的回答习惯。我们探讨何时不同的引出与读取答案的方式能够还原相同的判断，何时它们度量的只是一种回答习惯。我们在最多105个道德情境短文上收集了八个模型在六种语言中的110万条回复，变化了问题的形式、答案的约束方式以及回复的读取方式（标记或句子），涵盖两种措辞（即FAR-6测试组）。故事层面的判断画像在各种测试的读取方式和问题形式之间表现出收敛一致，唯一的例外是在否定疑问句之后按预设映射读取的是/否标记：在相同的回复上，标记画像与句子画像在各单元格中的中位数一致性为 r = 0.67，而句子画像与自由句子画像的一致性达到 0.94，后者属于已知的语言变异性。在去除每种语言的故事共识后，模型的画像最接近于其自身在……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 通过对八个模型、六种语言共110万条道德判断回复的分析，该研究发现除否定疑问句下按预设映射读取的“是/否”标记外，语言模型在不同提问形式和答案读取方式下均呈现一致的道德判断画像，表明多数测量方法反映的是真实判断而非回答习惯。
en_tdlr: Analyzing 1.1 million moral-judgment replies from eight models across six languages, this study shows that language models exhibit consistent judgment profiles across question forms and answer-reading methods—except for yes/no tokens read after negative interrogatives under preset mappings—indicating most elicitation methods measure genuine judgments rather than answering habits.
